analysis:
Both changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Server/NemotronSuperLocalHTTPReasoningToolTests.swift and NemotronSuperLocalHTTPTests.swift). No production code, attestation, key custody, WebSocket protocol, authorization or encryption paths are modified, so no threat-model assets (A-003, A-016 etc.) or boundaries (TB-002, TB-011) are directly affected.

ReasoningToolTests (head lines 110-123): adds coverage for response_format json_object combined with tools. Tool calls are returned as calls, JSON answers are validated, and non-JSON answers get 422. The previous test expected 400 for tools plus response_format. This implies production behavior elsewhere changed to permit the combination. That production change is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot assess it. The tests keep the existing negative cases: conflicting enable_thinking, logprobs, and literal <image> tag refusal. The tests use a loopback bearer token with no new network exposure.

LocalHTTPTests: removes the 8 MiB encoded-body refusal case (lines 250-260 base) and adds a comment saying the upload limit answers 413 first. This reduces a redundant test only. The upload limit is still tested in liveHTTPInlineImagesUseOwnerAndPreserveErrors (base line 152, expects contentTooLarge). Context-bound 400 refusals, zero reserved-budget checks, and the reset/retirement accounting tests are unchanged.

Remaining question for integration: the production change that loosens tools plus response_format validation is outside this batch. It should be reviewed for output validation and fail-closed behavior on malformed JSON. No finding is supported from this test-only evidence.
